title: 2025 Annual Australian Measles and Rubella Genotyping Surveillance Program Report.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Molecular characterisation is a critical component of Australia's measles and rubella surveillance systems, supporting outbreak investigations, identifying sources of infection, and providing evidence for the continued maintenance of Australia's measles and rubella elimination status.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This annual report summarises measles and rubella molecular epidemiology in Australia during 2025 and evaluates the utility of whole genome sequencing (WGS) for measles surveillance.
analysis.methods: In 2025, there were 181 confirmed measles cases notified in Australia, representing a 217.5% increase on the number notified in 2024. Rubella activity remained extremely low, with no rubella virus detections identified among 157 specimens tested by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and only two notified cases nationally, neither of which had material available for genotyping.
analysis.main_results: Measles virus genotypes B3 and D8 were detected, together with 21 vaccine-associated genotype A cases. Thirty-one epidemiologically confirmed outbreaks were identified, comprising 13 genotype B3 outbreaks and 17 genotype D8 outbreaks.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Genotype B3 predominated during the first half of the year and was largely associated with importations from Vietnam, whereas genotype D8 predominated during the second half of the year and was primarily associated with importations from Indonesia.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The discriminatory power and concordance with epidemiological data in the context of outbreak investigations was substantially greater for WGS data than for conventional N450-based genotyping. These findings support the continued absence of endemic measles and rubella transmission in Australia and highlight the value of WGS for enhancing measles surveillance and outbreak investigations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Viruses sharing the same N450-based distinct sequence identifier (DSid) differed by up to 33 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) for genotype B3 and 36 SNPs for genotype D8, whereas genomes obtained from epidemiologically linked cases differed by a maximum of four SNPs.

analysis.summary_en: This report provides an overview of the molecular epidemiology of measles and rubella in Australia during 2025. It highlights the increased number of measles cases compared to 2024, with genotypes B3 and D8 being detected. Genotype B3 was associated with importations from Vietnam, while genotype D8 was linked to Indonesia. The study also notes that no rubella virus was detected in 157 specimens tested by PCR, and only two rubella cases were reported. The findings indicate that measles cases were linked to importations rather than sustained endemic transmission. Whole genome sequencing (WGS) was found to have greater discriminatory power and concordance with epidemiological data compared to conventional N450-based genotyping. These results support the continued absence of endemic measles and rubella transmission in Australia and underscore the importance of WGS in improving measles surveillance and outbreak investigations.

title: Outcomes among Pregnant Women with Measles and Their Infants in the United States - Preliminary Analysis, 2025-2026.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the outcomes of pregnant women with measles and their infants during multiple large outbreaks from January 1, 2025, to September 28, 2026, given the known severe maternal and neonatal complications associated with measles during pregnancy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved 112 cases of confirmed measles during pregnancy and 13 cases of congenital measles reported to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, with complications including maternal pneumonia, preterm delivery, and neonatal complications.
analysis.methods: The study analyzed data from reported cases, focusing on maternal and neonatal outcomes, and highlighted the importance of MMR vaccination before pregnancy to prevent measles and related complications.
analysis.main_results: Almost all pregnant women with measles (98%) had not received MMR vaccination before pregnancy or had unknown vaccination status, and MMR vaccination before pregnancy and high community MMR vaccination coverage were found to be important to prevent measles and related complications.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings to emphasize the critical role of MMR vaccination before pregnancy in preventing measles and its complications, highlighting the need for improved vaccination coverage.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies to improve vaccination coverage and prevent maternal and neonatal complications from measles during pregnancy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the reliance on reported cases and the lack of detailed intervention protocols, but the evidence is strong for the importance of MMR vaccination before pregnancy.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed 112 cases of measles during pregnancy and 13 cases of congenital measles, highlighting the importance of MMR vaccination before pregnancy to prevent severe maternal and neonatal complications.

title: The historical evolution of measles treatment in Japan visualised through Japanese artwork and woodblock prints.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Measles epidemics recurred for centuries in Japan, and the study aimed to explore how historical visual culture mediated medical knowledge and public understanding during these periods.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was an interdisciplinary medical humanities analysis of Japanese visual materials, including kampō medical illustrations, hashika-e woodblock prints, and depictions of early quarantine practices, focusing on the 1862 measles outbreak and the Meiji-era transition to modern medicine.
analysis.methods: An interdisciplinary approach combining historical inquiry and qualitative visual analysis was used, with interpretations contextualised using contemporaneous writings and secondary scholarship.
analysis.main_results: Artistic media translated complex medical ideas into actionable household advice, commonly combining regimen guidance (notably diet and supportive care) with spiritual and talismanic protection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The visual record demonstrates a gradual shift from spiritual explanatory frameworks to modern scientific governance, including containment practices and vaccination-oriented prevention, offering a unique perspective on the co-evolution of measles management and public trust.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into how visual strategies can reinforce public confidence and cooperation in health measures, with implications for understanding historical public health communication and its relevance to contemporary disease prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on historical visual materials and secondary scholarship, which may introduce interpretive bias and limit the strength of causal inferences, though the evidence is contextualised within its historical framework.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the historical evolution of measles treatment in Japan through the lens of visual culture, particularly focusing on the 1862 measles outbreak and the Meiji-era transition to modern medicine. By analyzing kampō medical illustrations, hashika-e woodblock prints, and depictions of early quarantine practices, the research reveals how artistic media translated complex medical ideas into actionable household advice, often blending therapeutic regimens with spiritual and talismanic protection. The findings highlight a gradual shift from spiritual explanatory frameworks to modern scientific governance, including containment practices and vaccination-oriented prevention, offering a unique perspective on the co-evolution of measles management, culture, and public trust. The study's interdisciplinary approach, while insightful, is limited by its reliance on historical visual materials and secondary scholarship, which may introduce interpretive bias and reduce the strength of causal inferences. Nonetheless, the evidence provides a valuable understanding of how visual strategies have historically supported public health initiatives and can inform contemporary approaches to disease prevention and communication.

title: Fourteen years of measles surveillance in Sicily: epidemiological trends, adult susceptibility, and age-specific clinical profiles.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to describe measles epidemiology in Sicily over a 14-year period, addressing the ongoing public health concern of measles, particularly in high-income regions with insufficient vaccination coverage.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analysed laboratory-confirmed measles cases reported from July 2012 to May 2026 in Sicily, involving 1,169 cases across various demographics and healthcare settings.
analysis.methods: Cases were analysed using descriptive tests, univariate logistic regression, and phi coefficients to assess age-related associations and symptom co-occurrence.
analysis.main_results: The largest wave of cases occurred in 2018 (598 cases), with most patients being unvaccinated (93.5%) and adults accounting for 60.7% of cases, including 46 healthcare workers. Hospital-managed cases showed higher odds of complications, and the respiratory-mucosal pattern was more frequent in hospital-managed patients.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the re-emergence of measles and the need for high two-dose childhood coverage, catch-up vaccination for adolescents and adults, and systematic healthcare-worker immunity assessment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings underscore the persistent susceptibility across age groups and the necessity for laboratory-supported surveillance and targeted elimination strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the absence of randomization and potential bias due to the observational nature of the data, but the evidence is strong for the described trends and associations.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed 1,169 measles cases in Sicily from 2012 to 2026, revealing a significant wave in 2018 and highlighting the need for improved vaccination coverage and targeted interventions.

title: SVIR Model Analysis of Measles with Incomplete Vaccination and 1 Waning Immunity: Sidoarjo-Indonesia Case

analysis.research_question_and_background: The basicreproduction number R0 is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and the globalstability of both the disease-free and endemic equilibria is rigorously proven via Lyapunovfunctions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The supplied evidence does not clearly state the study design, setting, or study population.
analysis.methods: This study develops andanalyzes a Susceptible–Vaccinated–Infected–Recovered (SVIR) compartmental model formeasles transmission in Sidoarjo City, Indonesia, incorporating waning immunity.
analysis.main_results: Model parameters are estimated from weekly 2023 surveillance data in Sidoarjo Cityusing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Extended Kalman Filter, Maximum LikelihoodEstimation, and Least Squares, and evaluated via Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).PSO achieves the lowest MAPE (11.17%), outperforming the other methods.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The estimatedR0 = 0.668confirms a disease-free regime.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Measles remains a significant public health challenge in Indonesia, especially in regionswith heterogeneous vaccination coverage and waning immunity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Normalized sensitivity analysis identifies vaccineefficacy as the most influential parameter; a decline in efficacy to0 .75elevates R0 close tothe critical threshold, and any further reduction pushes the system into an endemic state.These findings underscore the necessity of maintaining high vaccine efficacy through boosterprograms and strengthened immunization strategies to sustain measles elimination at thedistrict level.

analysis.summary_en: The basicreproduction number R0 is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and the globalstability of both the disease-free and endemic equilibria is rigorously proven via Lyapunovfunctions. The supplied evidence does not clearly state the study design, setting, or study population. This study develops andanalyzes a Susceptible–Vaccinated–Infected–Recovered (SVIR) compartmental model formeasles transmission in Sidoarjo City, Indonesia, incorporating waning immunity. Model parameters are estimated from weekly 2023 surveillance data in Sidoarjo Cityusing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Extended Kalman Filter, Maximum LikelihoodEstimation, and Least Squares, and evaluated via Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).PSO achieves the lowest MAPE (11.17%), outperforming the other methods. The estimatedR0 = 0.668confirms a disease-free regime. Measles remains a significant public health challenge in Indonesia, especially in regionswith heterogeneous vaccination coverage and waning immunity. Normalized sensitivity analysis identifies vaccineefficacy as the most influential parameter; a decline in efficacy to0 .75elevates R0 close tothe critical threshold, and any further reduction pushes the system into an endemic state.These findings underscore the necessity of maintaining high vaccine efficacy through boosterprograms and strengthened immunization strategies to sustain measles elimination at thedistrict level.

title: Delayed Recognition of Measles Cluster Outbreaks in a High-Vaccination-Coverage Setting: Epidemiological and Clinical Characteristics of Primary and Index Cases with Different Immune Statuses, Henan Province, China, 2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: Background/Objectives: Under high measles vaccination coverage, breakthrough infections often present with mild, atypical features that may delay outbreak recognition.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We characterized measles cluster outbreaks in a high-coverage setting, focusing on the interval between primary-case and index-case onset as a measure of delayed outbreak recognition.
analysis.methods: We investigated three measles cluster outbreaks comprising 66 laboratory-confirmed cases reported in Henan Province, China, in 2025, using field investigation and laboratory testing, and compared clinical manifestations by immunization status; because of profound age differences between immunization groups, comparisons were presented descriptively.
analysis.main_results: The interval from primary- to index-case onset ranged from 4 to 15 days, representing an upper-bound estimate of the recognition delay. All three primary cases had received two doses of measles-containing vaccine (MCV) and presented with low-grade fever and localized rash, whereas none of the four index cases had an MCV history and all had peak temperatures ≥39 °C. Among cases with documented immunization history, pneumonia (17.4% vs. 37.5%) and hospitalization (43.5% vs. 62.5%) were less frequent in vaccinated than in unvaccinated cases; these unadjusted differences were confounded by age and are presented descriptively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Breakthrough measles infections in high-coverage settings have atypical presentation and mild symptoms. Such infections may lead to unrecognized community transmission.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Surveillance should incorporate active case finding for atypical presentations in high-coverage high-density settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The unadjusted differences were confounded by age, and the study focused on three outbreaks with limited generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated measles cluster outbreaks in Henan Province, China, in 2025, focusing on the delay in outbreak recognition. It found that the interval between primary-case and index-case onset ranged from 4 to 15 days, indicating a potential delay in identifying outbreaks. Primary cases, who had received two doses of measles-containing vaccine, presented with mild symptoms such as low-grade fever and localized rash, while index cases, who were unvaccinated, had more severe symptoms with peak temperatures ≥39 °C. The study also noted that vaccinated individuals had lower rates of pneumonia and hospitalization compared to unvaccinated individuals, though these differences were confounded by age. The findings highlight the atypical presentation of measles in high-vaccination settings and suggest the need for improved surveillance to detect such cases. The study's limitations include potential confounding by age and limited generalizability due to the small number of outbreaks analyzed.

title: An update to the critical vaccination threshold for measles herd immunity

analysis.research_question_and_background: Recent evidence indicates that measles vaccine-induced immunity may wane over time, challenging the classical assumption of lifelong protection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We develop a mathematical model of measles transmission and vaccination that explicitly incorporates waning immunity and derive updated expressions for the critical vaccination threshold ( $$p_c$$ ) and control reproduction number ( $$R_c$$ ), two cornerstone metrics used to guide public health vaccination policy.
analysis.methods: We additionally derive equations for outbreak probability and final outbreak size.
analysis.main_results: We apply the model to the 2024-2025 measles outbreak in the Southwestern Ontario Public Health Region and report ranges of the basic reproduction number ( $$R_0$$ ), outbreak peak timing and magnitude, final outbreak size, and the size of the population involved in transmission from feasible parameter sets that satisfy observed epidemic characteristics.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings suggest that widely used measles herd immunity thresholds may require re-evaluation in highly vaccinated populations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Specifically, under the model assumptions, we identify realistic parameter regimes in which vaccine-induced herd immunity cannot be achieved, despite high vaccine coverage.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Nevertheless, outbreak risk under these conditions may still remain very low.

analysis.summary_en: This study updates the critical vaccination threshold for measles herd immunity by incorporating waning immunity into a mathematical model. The research challenges the classical assumption of lifelong vaccine-induced protection and applies the model to the 2024-2025 measles outbreak in Southwestern Ontario. The findings reveal that even with slow waning immunity, herd immunity may not be achievable in highly vaccinated populations, suggesting the need for re-evaluation of current vaccination thresholds. The study also identifies parameter regimes where outbreak risk remains low despite high vaccine coverage. The evidence is based on a mathematical model and real-world outbreak data, with implications for public health policy. The analysis is grounded in the model's assumptions and observed epidemic characteristics, though the study does not provide detailed statistical methods or experimental validation.

title: Measles Vaccination, Population Immunity and Epidemiology in Northern Saudi Arabia: A Scoping Review with Cross-Border Context from Iraq and Jordan

analysis.scope_and_question: Measles remains an important vaccine-preventable infectious disease, particularly in populations with incomplete vaccination coverage, declining immunity, or surveillance systems that struggle to identify and respond to outbreaks. The purpose of this scoping review is to map and synthesize the available evidence on measles vaccination, population immunity, and epidemiology in Northern Saudi Arabia, with contextual consideration of relevant evidence from Iraq and Jordan.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review will follow the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews and will be reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The review will use the Population–Concept–Context (PCC) framework to guide eligibility criteria and evidence selection. The geographical focus will be Northern Saudi Arabia, particularly the Northern Borders, Al-Jouf, Ha'il, and Tabuk regions. Relevant data will be charted using a structured data-extraction approach and summarised descriptively and thematically. Eligible English-language publications from 1 January 2010 onwards will be considered.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Differences in vaccination uptake, population movement, access to healthcare, and the effectiveness of surveillance and outbreak-response activities may shape the distribution of measles susceptibility and outbreak risk. Findings will be presented using appropriate tables, narrative summaries, and geographical or thematic groupings where the available evidence permits. The review is expected to provide a structured overview of the available evidence on measles epidemiology, vaccination, and population immunity in Northern Saudi Arabia.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Geographical proximity alone does not establish cross-border transmission, and evidence from Iraq and Jordan will therefore be considered contextual rather than direct evidence of transmission into Saudi Arabia. The review will identify geographical, population-specific, methodological, and evidence gaps requiring further investigation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: A systematic mapping of the available evidence is needed to identify what is known about measles epidemiology, vaccination coverage, immunity, and surveillance in Northern Saudi Arabia, while highlighting relevant findings from Iraq and Jordan. This review will also identify geographical and thematic evidence gaps that may inform future research, public health planning, and immunization strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review aims to map and synthesize evidence on measles vaccination, population immunity, and epidemiology in Northern Saudi Arabia, with contextual insights from Iraq and Jordan. The review will use the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, focusing on Northern Borders, Al-Jouf, Ha'il, and Tabuk regions. It will examine measles incidence, prevalence, outbreak patterns, vaccination coverage, seroprevalence, and immunity gaps, while distinguishing contextual findings from direct evidence. The review will highlight geographical and thematic evidence gaps and provide a broader regional perspective on measles epidemiology and immunization challenges. However, it will not assume cross-border transmission based solely on geographical proximity. The findings are expected to support future research, public health planning, and immunization strategies in the region.

title: Sensitivity of Measles Real-time Reverse-transcription Polymerase Chain Reaction Testing During an Outbreak in Persons Without Rash.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the sensitivity of measles real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) testing in individuals exposed to measles but without rash during an outbreak, addressing the challenge of diagnosing measles in the absence of the characteristic rash.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted during the 2024 Chicago measles outbreak and involved 117 symptomatic persons with measles exposure but without rash, with 120 RT-PCR tests performed on them.
analysis.methods: Real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) testing was used to detect measles virus RNA in specimens from symptomatic individuals without rash, with testing repeated if initial results were negative.
analysis.main_results: The sensitivity of measles RT-PCR testing was reported as 78%, with 7 true positive results out of 120 tests performed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the importance of repeated testing in cases where initial results are negative, as measles can still be present in individuals without rash, which has implications for accurate diagnosis during outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform diagnostic protocols for measles in non-rash cases, improving surveillance and early detection during outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational nature and potential for false negatives, but the evidence is strong due to the direct observation of test results in a real-world outbreak setting.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the sensitivity of measles real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) testing in individuals exposed to measles but without rash during the 2024 Chicago outbreak. A total of 120 RT-PCR tests were conducted on 117 symptomatic individuals, yielding a sensitivity of 78% with 7 true positive results. The authors emphasize the need for repeated testing in such cases, as initial negative results do not rule out measles infection. The findings suggest that RT-PCR testing remains a valuable tool for diagnosing measles in non-rash presentations, which can improve surveillance and early detection during outbreaks. However, the study's observational design and potential for false negatives limit the confidence in its conclusions. The evidence is considered strong due to the direct observation of test results in a real-world outbreak setting.

title: Characterizing Measles Healthcare Facility Exposures-December 2023 Through September 2025: New York City.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to summarize exposures and transmission among people exposed to measles in healthcare settings in New York City (NYC) to address the common healthcare facility exposures and resource-intensive control measures required.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective descriptive study analyzed NYC Health Department's surveillance data of contacts exposed to measles cases in any NYC healthcare facility from December 2023 to September 2025.
analysis.methods: The study utilized NYC Health Department's surveillance data to analyze characteristics of contacts exposed to measles cases, including transmission, immunity status, postexposure prophylaxis (PEP) administration, facility setting, and time of exposure.
analysis.main_results: Of 2122 healthcare contacts to 28 cases, no secondary cases occurred. 1285 (60.6%) were vaccinated or had other evidence of immunity, 618 (29.1%) were adults with unknown immunity, 124 (5.8%) were not immune and received PEP, and 95 (4.5%) were not immune and did not receive PEP. Most contacts were exposed in emergency departments and/or hospital inpatient settings (1406; 66.3%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that most contacts exposed to measles in NYC healthcare facilities had presumptive immunity or were adults with unknown immunity, and no transmission occurred among 2122 exposed contacts, including nonimmune contacts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that relying solely on time-based measles exposure definitions may be overly broad and that incorporating strategies such as facility air exchange data might better assess transmission risk.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and the potential for unmeasured confounding factors. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed NYC Health Department's surveillance data of contacts exposed to measles in healthcare facilities from December 2023 to September 2025. No secondary cases occurred, and most contacts had presumptive immunity or unknown immunity, suggesting time-based exposure definitions may be overly broad.

title: Measles Update: Outbreaks, Vaccination Rates, Cost

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the resurgence of measles cases in 2026, highlighting the need for updated public health strategies to combat this highly contagious viral disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a descriptive analysis of measles outbreaks and vaccination rates across various regions in 2026, focusing on the global increase in cases and the associated public health challenges.
analysis.methods: The study compiles and analyzes global measles case data from public health reports and vaccination coverage statistics to identify trends and patterns in disease transmission and control.
analysis.main_results: The evidence reports that measles cases in 2026 are the highest in 35 years, indicating a significant resurgence of the disease.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the increase in cases as a reflection of declining vaccination rates and potential gaps in disease surveillance, emphasizing the novelty of the situation in the context of recent global health efforts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of maintaining high vaccination coverage and improving surveillance systems to prevent further outbreaks and mitigate the public health impact of measles.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on aggregated data and does not include detailed statistical analysis, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment based on the available evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study highlights the resurgence of measles cases in 2026, noting that they are the highest in 35 years. The research focuses on the global increase in measles outbreaks and the associated public health challenges, emphasizing the need for updated vaccination strategies and improved surveillance. The authors interpret the rise in cases as a result of declining vaccination rates and gaps in disease monitoring, which underscores the importance of maintaining high immunization coverage to prevent further spread. title: Mathematical Modelling of Measles Transmission with Alternative Childhood Vaccination-Entry Pathways in Kilifi County, Kenya: A Five-compartment Threshold, Sensitivity and Numerical Scenario Analysis

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how alternative childhood vaccination-entry pathways affect measles transmission dynamics, building on the established knowledge that measles transmission depends on susceptibility, the extent of childhood immunisation and the timing of vaccine receipt.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A deterministic five-compartment model was developed to investigate alternative vaccination-entry pathways using annual measles-related tabulations for children younger than ten years in Kilifi County, Kenya, during 2015–2024 as descriptive context and as numerical initial-state weights.
analysis.methods: The model comprises susceptible, delayed-entry vaccination, immediate-entry vaccination, infectious and recovered/immune classes. Positivity, boundedness, disease-free and endemic equilibria, local stability and normalised forward sensitivity were examined; adaptive Runge–Kutta integration was used to compare entry scenarios.
analysis.main_results: For the fixed theoretical baseline, the vaccination-adjusted reproduction threshold was Rv = 7.7534, the disease-free equilibrium was locally unstable and the positive endemic equilibrium was locally asymptotically stable. Recruitment and mass-action transmission each had elasticity + 1.0000, whereas immediate- and delayed-entry elasticities were -0.5791 and -0.2207. After nine years, the reference-scaled infectious state was 0.000922 without new entry, 0.000891 with delayed entry alone and 0.000845 with immediate entry alone.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The pathway classes are mathematical entry categories rather than measured distributions of vaccination delay. The matched-entry comparison demonstrates how overall entry intensity and pathway allocation exert different effects in this theoretical system.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform measles surveillance and vaccination strategies by highlighting the impact of different vaccination-entry pathways on disease transmission dynamics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is theoretical and based on a mathematical model, which may not fully capture real-world complexities. The evidence strength is moderate as it relies on simulated scenarios rather than empirical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study uses a deterministic five-compartment mathematical model to examine measles transmission dynamics in Kilifi County, Kenya, focusing on alternative childhood vaccination-entry pathways. The model incorporates susceptible, delayed-entry vaccination, immediate-entry vaccination, infectious and recovered/immune classes. The research highlights that the vaccination-adjusted reproduction threshold was Rv = 7.7534, with the disease-free equilibrium being locally unstable and the positive endemic equilibrium locally asymptotically stable. The results show that recruitment and mass-action transmission have an elasticity of +1.0000, while immediate- and delayed-entry elasticities were -0.5791 and -0.2207, respectively. After nine years, the reference-scaled infectious state was 0.000922 without new entry, 0.000891 with delayed entry alone, and 0.000845 with immediate entry alone. The study suggests that overall entry intensity and pathway allocation have different effects on disease transmission. The findings can inform measles surveillance and vaccination strategies, but the study is theoretical and based on simulated scenarios, limiting its evidence strength to moderate.

title: Assessment of progress of measles and rubella elimination strategies in the selected high risk areas of Chikkamagaluru district in Karnataka: a cross sectional study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the progress of measles and rubella elimination strategies in high-risk areas of Chikkamagaluru district, considering the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on vaccination coverage and surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted among children aged 1 to 5 years in selected high-risk areas of Chikkamagaluru district to evaluate measles-rubella (MR) elimination gaps. The study was carried out for one month.
analysis.methods: Data were collected through house-to-house visits using a pre-tested semi-structured questionnaire. Cluster sampling technique was employed to select the sample, which included 180 children.
analysis.main_results: The coverage of the 1st dose of the MR vaccine was 98.8%, while the coverage of the 2nd dose was 94.6%. The coverage of the 3rd dose of fractional IPV was 47.8%, with unavailability of fIPV being the main reason for missing this dose (74.5%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that the planning level assessment for measles and rubella elimination was satisfactory, indicating that the current strategies are on track to achieve the elimination goals.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the effectiveness of current measles and rubella elimination strategies in high-risk areas, which can inform targeted interventions to improve vaccination coverage and address gaps.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the potential for self-reporting bias. However, the evidence is strong as it is based on direct data collection from the target population.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study assessed measles and rubella elimination strategies in high-risk areas of Chikkamagaluru district, focusing on vaccination coverage among children aged 1 to 5 years. The study found that the first dose of the measles-rubella (MR) vaccine had a high coverage rate of 98.8%, while the second dose had a coverage of 94.6%. The third dose of fractional IPV had a lower coverage of 47.8%, primarily due to the unavailability of the vaccine. The authors concluded that the planning level assessment was satisfactory, suggesting that current strategies are effective. The study's findings highlight the importance of addressing gaps in vaccination coverage to achieve elimination goals. However, the study's cross-sectional design and potential for self-reporting bias limit the confidence in the results, though the evidence is considered strong due to direct data collection.

title: Kindergarten MMR Coverage, Vaccination Exemptions, and State-Level Measles Incidence in the United States, 2024 - 2026

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to examine associations of kindergarten measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) coverage and vaccination exemptions with state-level measles incidence in the United States during 2024-2026.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An ecological study was conducted across 50 states and Washington, DC, covering up to 153 jurisdiction-years, linking CDC surveillance, SchoolVaxView, and Census data.
analysis.methods: Negative-binomial models estimated incidence rate ratios (IRRs) per percentage-point increase for completed years 2024-2025 using generalized estimating equations and through MMWR week 39, 2024-2026 using maximum likelihood, adjusted for density and poverty.
analysis.main_results: Cases of measles rose from 269 in 2024 to 2,263 in 2025, with 3,642 reported provisionally through October 2, 2026. Completed-year IRRs were 0.875 (95% CI=0.806, 0.950) for MMR coverage, 1.202 (1.075, 1.344) for any exemption, and 1.207 (1.059, 1.376) for nonmedical exemption.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that higher exemption prevalence was associated with greater measles incidence, while other estimates were imprecise.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that monitoring vaccination exemptions alongside MMR coverage may help identify jurisdictions requiring closer assessment of vaccination gaps.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's ecological design does not establish causality, and the confidence in the results is moderate due to the limitations of observational data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the relationship between kindergarten measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccination coverage and exemptions with state-level measles incidence in the United States from 2024 to 2026. Using an ecological design, the researchers linked CDC surveillance, SchoolVaxView, and Census data across 50 states and Washington, DC. Negative-binomial models estimated incidence rate ratios (IRRs) per percentage-point increase in MMR coverage and exemptions, adjusting for density and poverty. The results showed a rise in measles cases from 269 in 2024 to 2,263 in 2025, with 3,642 provisional reports by October 2, 2026. Completed-year IRRs indicated that higher exemption prevalence was associated with increased measles incidence, while other estimates were imprecise. The study highlights the importance of monitoring vaccination exemptions alongside MMR coverage to identify jurisdictions needing closer assessment of vaccination gaps. However, the ecological design limits the ability to establish causality, and the confidence in the findings is moderate due to the observational nature of the data.

title: Determinants of measles vaccine hesitancy among caregivers of under five children in selected local government areas of Ogun State Nigeria

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify the determinants of measles vaccine hesitancy among caregivers of under-five children in Ogun State, Nigeria, as vaccine hesitancy has emerged as a major global public health challenge, undermining immunization programmes and contributing to the persistence of vaccine-preventable diseases despite the availability of effective vaccines.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A mixed-methods cross-sectional study was conducted among 368 caregivers selected using a multistage sampling technique. The study focused on caregivers with children aged 0–59 months who had resided in the study areas for at least six months and provided informed consent.
analysis.methods: Quantitative data were collected using structured questionnaires and analyzed using IBM SPSS version 27. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression were used to determine associations and predictors of vaccine hesitancy. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha, yielding a coefficient of 0.78.
analysis.main_results: The prevalence of vaccine hesitancy was 44.6%. Age group was significantly associated with vaccine hesitancy (p = 0.028), with younger caregivers more likely to be hesitant. However, knowledge (p = 0.774) and attitude (p = 0.442) were not significantly associated with vaccine hesitancy in multivariate analysis. Qualitative findings revealed substantial gaps in schedule-specific knowledge.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that measles vaccine hesitancy is significantly associated with structural, community, and interpersonal factors. The study demonstrated that vaccine hesitancy is a measurable and relevant challenge for childhood immunization, with caregivers’ knowledge, attitudes, and socio-demographic characteristics significantly associated with hesitancy and vaccination behavior.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted interventions to address structural, community, and interpersonal factors contributing to measles vaccine hesitancy, particularly in regions with relatively strong immunization infrastructure but persistent immunity gaps.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is context specific, and the achieved sample size of 368 would still provide adequate power (≥ 80%) to detect an odds ratio of 1.5 or greater for key predictors, assuming a design effect of up to 2.0. However, the study does not account for all potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the determinants of measles vaccine hesitancy among caregivers of under-five children in selected local government areas of Ogun State, Nigeria. A mixed-methods cross-sectional design was used, involving 368 caregivers surveyed through structured questionnaires and six focus group discussions. The quantitative analysis revealed a 44.6% prevalence of vaccine hesitancy, with younger caregivers more likely to be hesitant, while knowledge and attitude were not significant predictors. Qualitative findings highlighted gaps in schedule-specific knowledge. The authors interpreted these results as indicating that vaccine hesitancy is influenced by structural, community, and interpersonal factors. The study's findings are context-specific and suggest that interventions targeting these factors could improve vaccination rates. However, the study's limitations include the potential for unaccounted confounding factors and its focus on a specific geographic area.

title: Measles in Japan, as at May 2026

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the resurgence of measles in Japan following the relaxation of border control measures and to evaluate the impact of vaccination coverage on disease transmission. The background highlights the global decline in measles cases during the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent increase in reported cases since 2022.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed data from the National Epidemiological Surveillance of Infectious Diseases and the National Epidemiological Surveillance of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases in Japan, covering the period from 2008 to 2025. It included 265 measles cases reported in 2025, with a focus on vaccination status, travel history, and disease classification.
analysis.methods: The study utilized real-time RT-PCR testing for measles virus detection and genotyping of the N gene for viral identification. Measles antibody titers were measured using enzyme immunoassay (EIA) in 20 prefectures under the National Epidemiological Surveillance of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases.
analysis.main_results: In 2025, 265 measles cases were reported, with 194 cases having detectable viral genes and 186 cases having a determined genotype. Of these, 163 were genotype B3 and 23 were genotype D8. Additionally, 66 cases were suspected to have been infected overseas, while domestic infection was suspected in at least 60% of cases. The overall proportion of measles EIA antibody titers ≥2 was 96.1%, exceeding the 95% threshold required to prevent an epidemic.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the high proportion of antibody titers ≥2 as indicating sufficient immunity in the population to prevent an epidemic, despite the increase in measles cases. The study's novelty lies in its detailed analysis of measles genotypes and the association between travel history and infection sources in Japan.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform public health strategies by highlighting the importance of maintaining high vaccination coverage and strengthening surveillance systems to detect and respond to measles outbreaks effectively.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on statistical data from surveillance systems, which may be subject to underreporting or delays. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on reported cases and does not include direct clinical or biological data from individual patients.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the resurgence of measles in Japan following the lifting of border control measures for COVID-19 in 2023. It reports a significant increase in measles cases from 28 in 2023 to 265 in 2025, with a majority of cases classified as modified measles. The study highlights that 60% of cases were suspected to be domestically acquired, while 66 cases were linked to overseas travel. Despite a high proportion of measles antibody titers ≥2 (96.1%), vaccination coverage for both routine doses remained below the 95% target. The findings emphasize the need for improved vaccination rates and enhanced surveillance systems to prevent further outbreaks. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on reported cases and surveillance data, with limitations in direct clinical or biological analysis.

title: Measles: from elimination to resurgence. A literature review and current recommendations

analysis.scope_and_question: Measles virus (Morbillivirus hominis), historical taxonomic names, rubeola and measles disease. The review focuses on the epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of measles virus infections, with an emphasis on public health implications and the role of vaccination in controlling outbreaks.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a comprehensive analysis of literature, including clinical studies, epidemiological reports, and public health guidelines. It includes evidence from multiple sources, such as WHO recommendations, clinical case studies, and outbreak data. The review does not explicitly report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates but synthesizes findings from various studies to form a coherent overview of measles virus-related topics.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Measles is a highly contagious, vaccine-preventable viral disease caused by the measles virus, with a basic reproduction number of 12-18. It is transmitted via aerosolized respiratory droplets and presents with a characteristic prodrome followed by a maculopapular rash. Vitamin A supplementation is universally recommended for all diagnosed children, reducing childhood mortality by up to 62%. The MMR vaccine achieves 97% efficacy after two doses and requires population coverage above 93% to sustain herd immunity. Complications occur in approximately 30% of cases, with severe outcomes including pneumonia, acute encephalitis, and subacute sclerosing panencephalitis.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the importance of maintaining high vaccination rates to prevent outbreaks, but it does not provide specific data on the effectiveness of different vaccination strategies in diverse populations. There is also a lack of detailed information on the long-term effects of measles virus infections and the potential for resurgence in regions with low vaccination coverage. Additionally, the review does not address the role of specific measles virus genotypes in disease severity or transmission dynamics.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Global coordination, sustained vaccination campaigns, and heightened clinical awareness are essential to curb measles transmission. Research should focus on improving vaccination strategies, particularly in vulnerable populations such as children under 5, young adults without prior immunization, pregnant women, and immunocompromised individuals. Surveillance and diagnostic methods should be enhanced to ensure timely identification and management of measles cases. Post-exposure prophylaxis with MMR vaccine within 72 hours or immunoglobulin within 6 days is recommended for high-risk individuals.

analysis.summary_en: This review provides an overview of measles virus, emphasizing its epidemiology, clinical presentation, and public health significance. It highlights the importance of vaccination in preventing outbreaks and reducing mortality, particularly through vitamin A supplementation. The review underscores the need for global coordination and sustained vaccination efforts to maintain herd immunity. However, it notes gaps in understanding the long-term effects of measles infections and the role of specific genotypes in disease outcomes. Research and practice implications include improving vaccination strategies, enhancing surveillance, and ensuring timely post-exposure prophylaxis for high-risk groups.

title: Transmission‐Based Infection Control Preparedness in Dentistry: Lessons From Andes Virus, Measles, and Ebola Epidemics

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore preparedness for transmission-based infection control in dentistry by drawing lessons from the Andes virus, measles, and Ebola epidemics. The background highlights the historical context of these viral outbreaks and their implications for public health.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study design involved a review of existing literature and case studies from the Andes virus, measles, and Ebola epidemics, focusing on transmission-based infection control measures.
analysis.methods: The methods included a comprehensive review of the literature, analysis of case studies, and identification of key lessons for improving infection control in dental settings.
analysis.main_results: The study found that lessons from the Andes virus, measles, and Ebola epidemics could be applied to enhance transmission-based infection control in dentistry, emphasizing the importance of strict hygiene protocols, personal protective equipment, and rapid response systems.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as novel insights into the application of historical epidemic lessons to modern dental practice, highlighting the need for continuous improvement in infection control measures.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings could inform the development of more robust infection control protocols in dental settings, potentially reducing the risk of transmission of infectious diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the reliance on historical case studies and the potential for bias in the interpretation of lessons learned. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study reviewed lessons from the Andes virus, measles, and Ebola epidemics to enhance transmission-based infection control in dentistry, emphasizing the need for strict hygiene protocols and rapid response systems.

title: Perfil epidemiológico da reemergência do sarampo no Brasil (2015-2025)

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to analyze the epidemiological profile of measles re-emergence in Brazil between 2015 and 2025, considering incidence, mortality, vaccination coverage, and regional and demographic distribution.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective, descriptive, ecological time-series study using DATASUS data was conducted in Brazil, focusing on the period from 2015 to 2025.
analysis.methods: Incidence, mortality, vaccination coverage, and epidemiological profiles were analyzed according to demographic and regional variables using descriptive statistics, Prais-Winsten regression, Spearman correlation, and comparisons between epidemiological phases.
analysis.main_results: A resurgence in incidence occurred starting in 2018, peaking at 10.47 cases per 100,000 inhabitants in 2019. Phase 2 (2018–2020) saw the highest incidence rates, marking the primary critical period of re-emergence. A heterogeneous distribution was observed, with greater vulnerability in the North region, higher occurrence among children aged 0 to 4 years, and a concentration of deaths between 2018 and 2021. Vaccination coverage showed a downward trend for both the first and second doses of the MMR (measles, mumps, and rubella) and MMRV (measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella) vaccines.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrated a temporal coexistence between declining vaccination coverage and the resurgence of measles incidence, within a context of regional heterogeneity and persistent epidemiological conditions favorable to new outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The correlation between vaccination coverage and incidence was negative but not statistically significant, highlighting the need for targeted interventions to address regional disparities and improve vaccination rates.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on ecological data and the lack of statistical significance in the correlation between vaccination coverage and incidence, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the epidemiological profile of measles re-emergence in Brazil from 2015 to 2025, focusing on incidence, mortality, vaccination coverage, and regional and demographic distribution. A significant resurgence in cases was observed starting in 2018, peaking in 2019, with higher incidence rates in the North region and among children aged 0 to 4 years. Vaccination coverage for both the first and second doses of MMR and MMRV vaccines showed a downward trend. The study highlights the coexistence of declining vaccination rates and increased measles cases, emphasizing the need for targeted public health interventions. However, the correlation between vaccination coverage and incidence was not statistically significant, which limits the strength of the evidence. The findings underscore the importance of addressing regional disparities and maintaining vaccination efforts to prevent future outbreaks.

title: District immunization coverage before, during and after the 2023 big catch-up in Sierra Leone: an ecological analysis of routine administrative data and population denominators, 2020 to 2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess how immunization coverage in Sierra Leone’s districts changed before, during and after the 2023 Big Catch-Up, and how the denominators influenced these results.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An ecological analysis was conducted using routine administrative data from 1,536 district and 96 national DHIS2 records across 16 indicators in Sierra Leone from 2020 to 2025.
analysis.methods: District-clustered Poisson generalized estimating equations compared 2023 with 2020 to 2022, and 2024 to 2025 with 2023. Between-district differences in fully immunized child and measles second-dose coverage were measured using standard deviation and population-weighted Gini coefficient (bootstrap intervals).
analysis.main_results: National fully immunized child coverage increased from 86.5% (2020 to 2022) to 106.4% in 2023 (rate ratio 1.23, 95% confidence interval 1.12 to 1.36) and remained at 108.1% in 2025. The lowest district value rose from 67.3% in 2022 to 84.9% in 2025, with the four lowest districts reporting 110% to 121%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The 2023 Big Catch-Up was associated with increased recorded immunization activity, and post-catch-up coverage changes were closely linked to revisions of the population projections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Administrative coverage should be interpreted alongside recorded counts and dose-completion ratios, while strengthening routine measles second-dose and birth-dose vaccination remains a priority.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study relied on routine administrative data and the interpretation of coverage above 100% depended on how it was treated.

analysis.summary_en: This ecological analysis examined measles immunization coverage in Sierra Leone’s 16 districts before, during, and after the 2023 Big Catch-Up, using routine administrative data from 2020 to 2025. The study found that national fully immunized child coverage increased significantly in 2023 and remained elevated in 2025, with some districts showing marked improvements. The Gini coefficient, which measures inequality in coverage, decreased when coverage above 100% was capped. The findings suggest that the 2023 campaign boosted immunization activity, but the interpretation of coverage changes depended on how data were handled. The study highlights the importance of considering recorded counts and dose-completion ratios alongside administrative coverage metrics. However, the reliance on routine data and the impact of denominator adjustments limit the confidence in the results, making the evidence strength moderate.

title: Childhood Vaccination Coverage and Adult Immunization Policy: An Exploratory Comparison of Egypt, Canada, and the United States

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to explore whether childhood vaccination coverage rankings align with the documented breadth of adult immunization policy across three countries.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was an exploratory comparison of childhood vaccination coverage in Egypt, Canada, and the United States using data from 2015 to 2024.
analysis.methods: The analysis involved descriptive statistics and ordinary least-squares trends with Newey-West standard errors (lag 1), alongside sensitivity analyses using t-based intervals and Holm adjustment for six tests.
analysis.main_results: Egypt had the highest mean coverage for both DTP3 (95.2%) and MCV1 (94.9%), followed by the United States (94.1% and 91.6%) and Canada (91.5% and 90.4%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that childhood coverage rankings did not align with the documented breadth of adult immunization policy, highlighting the need for separate reporting of childhood coverage and adult dimensions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that adult vaccination policy documentation and uptake measurement differ substantially, which has implications for understanding and improving national immunization systems.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was descriptive and did not test predictive relationships or establish statistical associations, which limits the strength of the evidence and the conclusions that can be drawn.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores whether childhood vaccination coverage rankings align with the documented breadth of adult immunization policy in Egypt, Canada, and the United States. Using data from 2015 to 2024, the authors found that Egypt had the highest coverage for both DTP3 and MCV1 vaccines, followed by the United States and Canada. They calculated descriptive statistics and ordinary least-squares trends with Newey-West standard errors, and conducted sensitivity analyses using t-based intervals and Holm adjustment. The authors concluded that childhood coverage rankings did not align with adult policy breadth, emphasizing the need for separate reporting of childhood and adult vaccination metrics. The study's descriptive nature limits its ability to establish statistical associations or predictive relationships, and the results cannot be used to rank the overall performance of national immunization systems. The findings have implications for understanding the differences in adult vaccination policy documentation and uptake measurement across countries.

title: Timing of de novo vaccination during pregnancy impacts maternal and newborn immunity

analysis.research_question_and_background: Maternal immunity is essential for protecting both the pregnant individual and fetus, balancing immune tolerance with defense against infection. While maternal vaccination enhances protection, the impact of gestational timing on antibody responses and transplacental antibody transfer remains unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: To investigate how vaccination timing shapes maternal and fetal immunity, we performed comprehensive serological profiling in 263 individuals, including 96 maternal–neonatal dyads, sampled across pregnancy and at delivery.
analysis.methods: Leveraging natural variation in SARS-CoV-2 vaccine timing, we assessed antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 and 13 additional pathogens using Systems Serology, analyzing isotypes, subclasses, FcγR binding, glycosylation, neutralization, and Fc-mediated functions.
analysis.main_results: Antibody transfer was most efficient following late second to early third trimester vaccination, with decreased transfer in the late third trimester. Fetal sex also influenced antibody transfer efficiency, favoring male fetuses in the third trimester.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings underscore the importance of vaccine timing to optimize maternal and neonatal immunity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings cautiously inform the timing of vaccination during pregnancy to enhance antibody transfer to the fetus, particularly for male fetuses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength for the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how the timing of vaccination during pregnancy affects maternal and fetal immunity. The research focuses on antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 and other pathogens, using Systems Serology to analyze various immune parameters. The main results show that antibody transfer is most efficient when vaccination occurs in the late second to early third trimester, with decreased transfer in the late third trimester. Fetal sex also influenced antibody transfer efficiency, with male fetuses showing higher transfer rates. The findings highlight the importance of vaccine timing to optimize immunity for both the mother and the newborn. The study's implications suggest that adjusting vaccination schedules during pregnancy could enhance protection for the fetus. The evidence is based on serological profiling of 263 individuals, including 96 maternal–neonatal dyads, and the results are interpreted within the context of immune responses. The study's design and methods are described, but no specific limitations are reported.

title: Sarampión: de la eliminación al rebrote. Revisión de la literatura y recomendaciones actuales

analysis.research_question_and_background: El sarampión es una enfermedad viral altamente contagiosa, prevenible por vacunación y de notificación obligatoria, que representa un problema de salud pública vigente.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Su agente causal es el virus del sarampión (familia Paramyxoviridae), de serotipo único, transmitido por vía aérea con un número reproductivo básico de 12 a 18.
analysis.methods: La presentación clínica clásica incluye un pródromo de fiebre, tos, coriza y conjuntivitis, seguido de las manchas de Koplik y un exantema maculopapular cefalocaudal.
analysis.main_results: El diagnóstico se confirma mediante serología (IgM específica), reacción en cadena de la polimerasa o cultivo viral.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: El tratamiento es fundamentalmente de soporte; en pacientes pediátricos, la vitamina A reduce la mortalidad hasta un 62%, por lo que está recomendada por la OMS en este grupo de pacientes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Las complicaciones ocurren en aproximadamente el 30% de los casos; las más frecuentes son diarrea (8%) y otitis media (7-9%), y las complicaciones graves incluyen neumonía, diarrea, encefalitis aguda, encefalomielitis aguda posinfecciosa y, a largo plazo, panencefalitis esclerosante subaguda.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Las poblaciones más vulnerables son los menores de 5 años, los adultos jóvenes sin inmunización previa, las embarazadas y los inmunocomprometidos.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the ongoing public health problem of measles, emphasizing its high contagiousness, prevention through vaccination, and the need for continuous surveillance. The research highlights the clinical presentation of measles, including the characteristic prodrome and rash, and outlines diagnostic methods such as serology, PCR, and viral culture. It also discusses the importance of supportive treatment, particularly the role of vitamin A in reducing mortality among pediatric patients. The study notes that complications occur in about 30% of cases, with common issues like diarrhea and otitis media and severe outcomes such as pneumonia and subacute sclerosing panencephalitis. Vulnerable populations include children under five, unvaccinated adults, pregnant women, and immunocompromised individuals. The paper underscores the critical role of vaccination coverage, with the triple viral vaccine showing 97% efficacy after two doses and requiring over 93% population coverage for herd immunity. It also references the significant decline in vaccination coverage in Mexico, leading to over 12,000 confirmed cases and more than 33 deaths during the 2025-2026 outbreak, primarily affecting unvaccinated children. The study concludes that global coordination, sustained vaccination campaigns, and enhanced clinical vigilance remain essential to control transmission.

title: Comparative Performance of CNN and HOG-LBP-Based SVM for Mpox Classification

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to compare the performance of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) using combined Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) and Local Binary Patterns (LBP) features for binary classification of mpox and other skin lesion images. Skin lesions caused by mpox may visually resemble those resulting from other skin diseases, making image-based classification a potential approach to support preliminary screening.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study compared the performance of a CNN and an SVM using a dataset of 224 unique original images, comprising 116 mpox images and 108 images of other conditions, including chickenpox and measles. The models were evaluated using identical stratified five-fold cross-validation partitions.
analysis.methods: The experimental dataset consisted of 224 unique original images, and the models were evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and specificity. The SVM employed a 23,250-dimensional HOG-LBP feature vector with a Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel, whereas the CNN automatically learned visual representations from preprocessed RGB images.
analysis.main_results: The CNN achieved an average accuracy of 84.37%, precision of 88.73%, recall of 80.25%, F1-score of 84.06%, and specificity of 88.92%, while the SVM achieved 83.03%, 84.87%, 81.92%, 83.32%, and 84.28%, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results indicate that the CNN achieved higher performance in four evaluation metrics, while the SVM obtained slightly higher recall. These findings demonstrate that both approaches offer different classification strengths within the evaluated dataset.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that both CNN and SVM can be effective for mpox classification, with CNN showing superior performance in most metrics. Further evaluation using independent datasets and more diverse skin lesion images is necessary to assess their generalizability before potential application in preliminary mpox screening.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by the use of a relatively small and specific dataset.

analysis.summary_en: This study compared the performance of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) for classifying mpox and other skin lesions. The CNN outperformed the SVM in most metrics, but further evaluation is needed to confirm generalizability.

title: Perception of Socio-Cultural and Socio-Demographic Determinants ofVaccine-Preventable Disease Occurrence Among Mothers of Under-Five Children in Ilorin West Local Government Area, Kwara State

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the socio-cultural and socio-demographic determinants of vaccine-preventable disease occurrence among mothers of under-five children in Ilorin West Local Government Area, Kwara State, Nigeria.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A quantitative descriptive survey was conducted among mothers of children under five years old residing in Ilorin West Local Government Area, Kwara State, Nigeria, with a total of 418 respondents selected through a multistage sampling procedure.
analysis.methods: Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analysed with descriptive statistics and chi-square tests at a 0.05 alpha level.
analysis.main_results: Mothers reported that measles (21.3%) and pertussis (16.3%) were perceived as prevalent among their children, with a pooled affirmative response rate of 9.1% across seven disease items. They also held moderately positive socio-cultural beliefs and practices favouring immunisation, with a grand mean of 2.68/4.00, and perceived sociodemographic factors such as maternal education, household income, and antenatal care attendance as linked to VPD occurrence, with a grand mean of 2.76/4.00.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights that socio-cultural and socio-demographic factors are perceived as significant determinants of vaccine-preventable disease occurrence in the region, offering new insights into the local context of immunisation practices.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted public health interventions to address vaccine hesitancy and improve immunisation coverage in Ilorin West Local Government Area, particularly by addressing socio-demographic and cultural barriers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on self-reported data and perceptions, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on survey data rather than direct biological or clinical measurements.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the socio-cultural and socio-demographic determinants of vaccine-preventable disease occurrence among mothers of under-five children in Ilorin West Local Government Area, Kwara State, Nigeria. A quantitative descriptive survey design was used, involving 418 mothers selected through multistage sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analysed with descriptive statistics and chi-square tests. Mothers reported measles and pertussis as prevalent diseases, with a pooled response rate of 9.1%. They also held moderately positive beliefs about immunisation and perceived sociodemographic factors as linked to disease occurrence. The study suggests that these factors are influential in shaping perceptions of vaccine-preventable disease burden. The findings can inform public health strategies to address vaccine hesitancy and improve immunisation rates. However, the reliance on self-reported data introduces potential bias, limiting the strength of the evidence.
